58-- Harness prompts require the published build and binary to run and measurements to come from their OUTPUT. Scripts must never parse or assert on source text. Measurement checks fail only on missing or invalid output; deterministic scoring owns anchor comparisons.
59-- Without `args.harness_from`, there is one initial agent call (`harness`, `ls-writer`, `sonnet`). Setup permits up to four repairs (`harness-repair`) and anchors up to two (`anchors-repair`) after a nonzero exit, with the same role/model. Each repair receives the failure class and at most the last 200 log lines of the latest failed attempt, and its prompt states its attempt number and the step's limit (`repair attempt <n> of <limit>`). Each later repair runs only after the previous repaired script ran and failed again (nonzero exit or output-gate error); a declined (null) repair, an infrastructure or fetch failure, or a failed upload ends the step. Owner direction 2026-10-30: finish experiments rather than stop them on a fixable failure; a blind run spent its one setup repair on a build-dependency failure, the repair worked, and setup then failed on a different import error that a single repair could not reach. U46 run evidence (blind-01 run7, 2026-10-31): setup spent both of its two repairs on successive script errors; each repair's log tail held its error, each repair targeted it and none regressed, a static check before upload would have caught none, and setup reruns reuse the materials already fetched and verified, so an attempt after a repair costs tens of seconds; an authorized reader judged more repairs of the same kind the smallest sufficient fix. Anchors keep two repairs until a run shows otherwise. The setup repair may rewrite only `setup.sh`. The anchors step executes `run_anchors.sh` and the `run_command.sh` it invokes, so the anchors repair may rewrite either or both and nothing else; a rewritten `run_command.sh` still obeys every `run_command.sh` rule above, and the anchors repair prompt states this. After each repair every rewritten script is recopied, then the step reruns once, with its budget resolved at the rerun's start (U47). Under reuse, an accepted anchors repair marks `modified` true for each of the two scripts whose bytes it changed. Infrastructure/fetch failures do not trigger repairs. Timeouts use the same repairs (the step's own limit), never an extra one. Repair prompts include budget seconds, measured wall seconds and max(0, wall_s-budget_s) overrun seconds. Profiling has no agent repair or execution retry; output/gate failures stop downstream work.

61-## A/results/reproduce/ and deterministic anchor scoring
62-- Every reproduce box command fetches remote `out/` into `A/results/reproduce/out/`, and its `<receipt-id>.log` into `A/results/reproduce/`. Logs remain in the agent view. The local fetched `out/` is cleared before each command to prevent stale measurements. The final copy contains the anchor run's outputs. When reproduce passes, the pipeline freezes those outputs on the box: through boxrun, as operation `reproduce-freeze` under the `setup` budget, it runs `test ! -e reproduce-out` and then `cp -a out reproduce-out` in the shared run directory. Like every reproduce command, its fetch replaces `A/results/reproduce/out/`, so that local copy and remote `reproduce-out/` hold the same outputs: the baseline outputs the seal and the test author read. Later stages never write to `reproduce-out/`; remote `out/` after reproduce also collects profiler and probe outputs and further runs of the baseline command, which are not baseline outputs. A failed `reproduce-freeze` (nonzero exit, failed fetch, or timeout) fails reproduce with `error_class: infra`, or `timeout` on a timeout, without repair.
63-- `python3 m5/score_anchors.py <anchors.json> <measured.json> <out.json>` writes an atomic JSON object with exact keys `anchors`, `anchors_passed`, `anchors_total`, `all_passed`, `references_total`.
64-  - `anchors` preserves intake order and contains `{id, kind, published_value, measured_value, tolerance, passed}` for every item, with `kind` `"anchor"` or `"reference"`. Items with `uncertainty` keep it unchanged in their row. Reference rows have `passed: null` and `difference` (measured minus published, or null when unmeasured); an unmeasured reference row has `reason` `missing` or `non_numeric` and is never a failure. `tolerance` preserves its input form; `passed` is boolean. Missing or non-numeric measurements are represented by `measured_value: null`. Failed rows additionally contain `reason`: `unknown_comparison`, `missing`, `non_numeric`, `out_of_tolerance` (for `"=="`), or `threshold_not_met` (for inequalities). Unknown comparisons take precedence over measurement failures; missing measurements take precedence over non-numeric measurements. Passing rows have no `reason` field.
65-  - `anchors_passed` and `anchors_total` count anchors only and `references_total` counts references; all are nonnegative integers. `all_passed` is true exactly when every anchor passed, including when there are none. An empty array is valid. Duplicate IDs, invalid published values, invalid tolerances or uncertainties, and nonfinite calculated equality differences/tolerances are parse errors. Unknown comparisons and missing/non-numeric measurements are anchor failures rather than parse errors.
66-  - Exit 0 means every anchor passed; exit 4 means at least one anchor failed; exit 1 means invalid/missing input or an output write failure. Invalid input does not produce a new score file. Diagnostics contain no input content.
67-- The pipeline writes the score to `A/results/reproduce/anchors_scored.json`.
68-- Reproduce facts are `{anchors_passed, anchors_total, stock_verified, tuned_control_valid}` plus common `tokens_known` and `gpu_busy_known`. Counts remain null until scoring succeeds; `stock_verified` is true only after setup exits 0; `tuned_control_valid` remains null. The gate passes only when stock is verified and every anchor passes (true with no anchors). `run_valid` is true/false when anchor scoring passes/fails with at least one anchor, and null when there are no anchors.

70:## Unit equivalence check (U51)
71-- Purpose: before any spend on concurrency, test whether `run_units.sh` reproduces the measured baseline's own per-unit result files, at the earliest point a run can (about one hour after the box starts instead of after reproduce and profile). Owner direction 2026-11-01: test equivalence before spending on concurrency; keep a failed comparison as recorded and never change its criterion after observing it; distinguish ordinary run-to-run variability from an effect of subsetting. The comparison is against a recorded measured baseline, with that baseline's existing limits.
72-- Optional `args.units_check` is an object with exactly the key `reference`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a local directory of a previous run's recorded baseline outputs (its `A/results/reproduce/out/`). An invalid value fails reproduce with `error_class: parse` before any box command. Without `args.units_check`, reproduce and every later stage are unchanged.
73-- In units-check mode reproduce runs the box probe, harness copy or generation, upload and setup with its repairs exactly as usual. After the harness copy, `A/harness/` must hold `run_units.sh` and a `units.json` valid as defined under "A/harness/" with at least four units; otherwise reproduce fails with `error_class: parse` before the harness upload. After setup passes, the check runs in place of the usual anchors step:
74-  1. Sample: the four units chosen by the unit-mode sample rule (see Concurrency probe), in sample order.
75-  2. Subset run: through boxrun, as operation `units-check` under the resolved `anchors` budget, from the shared run directory, one command that removes any earlier `units-check/` and `out/units-check/`; builds a fresh `units-check/` work directory holding a symlink to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work`, `evaluation-work` and `units-check`, plus an empty `out/`; runs `bash harness/run_units.sh <id0> <id1> <id2> <id3>` there with stdout and stderr in `out/units-check/run.log` of the shared run directory; writes the invocation's own monotonic wall seconds to `out/units-check/wall.json` as `{"wall_s": <seconds>}`; copies the work directory's `out/` contents to `out/units-check/files/`, also when the invocation failed; and exits with the invocation's exit status. The command is authored work: no repair and no identical retry. A timeout or infrastructure failure fails reproduce with `timeout` or `infra` as usual.
76-  3. Comparison, local, before any later reproduce command: the fetched `out/units-check/` is copied to `A/results/reproduce/units-check/`. For every output path of every sample unit, the file under `A/results/reproduce/units-check/files/` must be byte-identical to the same path under `reference`; a file missing on either side is a mismatch. `subset_match` is true exactly when the invocation exited 0 and every file matched.
77-  4. Variability control: only when the invocation exited 0 and `subset_match` is false, the usual anchors step then runs once as specified above (`run_anchors.sh` with its repairs and scoring), and afterwards the same sample units' files in the fetched full-run `A/results/reproduce/out/` are compared byte for byte with `reference` (`full_match`) and with the saved subset files (`subset_vs_full_match`). Otherwise the anchors step does not run.
78-- `A/results/reproduce/units_check.json` is written atomically with exactly `{sample, subset_rc, subset_wall_s, cost_sum_s, cost_ratio, files_total, files_matched, subset_match, full_ran, full_match, subset_vs_full_match}`: `sample` is four rows `{index, cost_s}` (manifest position and recorded cost); `subset_rc` the invocation's integer exit status; `subset_wall_s` from `wall.json`, a finite positive number or null when unavailable; `cost_sum_s` the sum of the sample's `cost_s`; `cost_ratio` = `subset_wall_s / cost_sum_s`, or null; `files_total` and `files_matched` count the sample's output paths and the matches; `subset_match` a boolean; `full_ran` a boolean; `full_match` and `subset_vs_full_match` booleans, or null when the full run did not run or did not exit 0. No unit identifier or output path appears in the file.
79-- Reproduce facts add optional `units_match` (the file's `subset_match`) and `units_full_match` (its `full_match`), each a boolean or null; both are null outside units-check mode and on SKIPPED/stub records, and records without them stay valid. In units-check mode reproduce never runs `reproduce-freeze`. Its status is PASS once setup passed and `units_check.json` was written, whatever the comparison found; when the variability-control anchors step ran, the status follows the usual anchors rules instead. In units-check mode every stage after reproduce except takeaways is SKIPPED, as after a failed stage.

81-## A/results/profile/ and A/profile-packet.json
82-- Profile fetches remote `out/` to `A/results/profile/out/`; logs are `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. Its inputs are therefore under `A/results/profile/out/profile/`. Remote `out/profile/` is cleared before profiling to prevent stale evidence from passing.
83-- The pipeline uploads trusted `m5/profile_nsys.sh`, `m5/profile_summarise.py` and the collected probe into remote `profiler/`. Through boxrun, it invokes `bash profiler/profile_nsys.sh harness/run_command.sh out/profile <budget_s>`. The profiler reuses `nsys` from PATH or NVIDIA installation paths. Otherwise it tries `nsight-systems-cli` with apt using only source files listed by the probe, without enabling commented repositories or adding sources. If unavailable, it downloads the official Ubuntu 22.04 amd64 CLI package `NsightSystems-linux-cli-public-2025.3.1.90-3582212.deb` from `https://developer.download.nvidia.com/devtools/repos/ubuntu2204/amd64/` into a temporary directory outside `out/` that is removed after installation (the package never reaches `out/` or fetched results), verifies the SHA-256 pinned in the script, installs with `sudo -n dpkg -i` and runs `sudo -n apt-get -f install -y` for dependencies using the image's existing sources without adding repositories. This fixed profiler installation is an exception to the setup-script installation restrictions above. The profiler prepends the discovered Nsight binary directory to PATH. Missing tools, installation failures and collection/export failures emit `M5_PROFILER_INFRA`, write `out/profile/infra.json`, and exit 2; the pipeline classifies these as `infra` without agent calls.
84-- Collection uses `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none` around the shared command without modifying its environment. An inner launcher measures only that command with a monotonic clock; installation, profiler finalization and CSV export are excluded. The command's output is preserved in `baseline.log` as well as its own saved logs. Export uses `nsys stats --report cuda_gpu_kern_sum,cuda_gpu_mem_time_sum,cuda_api_sum --format csv`. Raw report, CSV files, tool version, export log, `raw_wall_s.json` and `gpu_util_raw.jsonl` remain in `out/profile/`.
85-- `python3 m5/profile_summarise.py <out_dir>` deterministically writes the three existing profile files. CSV total time/duration units ns, us/µs, ms and s are converted to seconds. Known Nsight skips for absent kernel/memory/API activity count as zero; missing or malformed reports fail parsing. A report is a known skip when its CSV file carries Nsight's `SKIPPED` line and no header row, or when its CSV file is absent, empty or whitespace-only and `stats.log` in the same directory states that the report does not contain its own activity: `does not contain CUDA kernel data` for `stats_cuda_gpu_kern_sum.csv`, `does not contain GPU memory data` for `stats_cuda_gpu_mem_time_sum.csv`, and `does not contain CUDA trace data` for `stats_cuda_api_sum.csv` (U48). These are Nsight's own wordings; the earlier phrases `CUDA memory data` and `CUDA API data` never occur in Nsight output and no longer count as statements. Nsight Systems 2025 writes an empty file for a skipped report where earlier versions wrote none. An absent, empty or whitespace-only file without that statement for its own activity, and any other missing or malformed report, still fails parsing. Run evidence (blind-01 run9, 2026-11-01): the baseline ran to completion under the profiler with no CUDA activity and no capture problem; Nsight 2025 logged the three skips and wrote three empty summary files, and the summariser failed on a missing CSV header, so profile stopped with `parse` instead of reaching its numeric gate. Replay of the merged U48 summariser on run9's saved files (2026-11-01) still failed: Nsight states the memory and API skips as `GPU memory data` and `CUDA trace data`; with those wordings the summariser exits 0 and the gate reports `numeric` (other host time within 2% of total wall). Five rows are emitted: `kernels` (compute), `memcpy H2D` (transfer), `memcpy D2H` (transfer), `CUDA API host time` (other), and `other host time` (other). GPU seconds retain the raw kernel/transfer sums; host GPU seconds are null. Aggregate CSV reports do not identify critical-path intervals: if the four reported sums exceed measured wall, their wall allocations are scaled proportionally to fit. Other host time is the nonnegative wall remainder. These allocations are an aggregate approximation, not measured exclusive phase durations. No stage timestamps are invented; aggregate rows omit `start_s`, so stage utilisation remains null. No bound uses stage utilisation; same-GPU headroom comes from the concurrency probe.
86-- `stages.json` is an array of `{stage, wall_s, gpu_s}`, optionally including `kind`: `compute`, `transfer`, or `other`, and `start_s`: finite nonnegative elapsed seconds sharing the telemetry clock. Fixed profiler supplies `kind`; legacy rows without it remain accepted. `stage` is a non-empty string; `wall_s` is finite nonnegative seconds; `gpu_s` is finite nonnegative seconds or null and must be present. Fixed profiler wall allocations sum to measured wall without exceeding it; overlapping aggregate durations use the approximation above. Extra input fields are not copied to the packet. Empty arrays parse but fail the numeric gate.
87-- `total_wall_s.json` is an object with finite positive numeric `total_wall_s` in seconds. The sum of stage wall times must also be finite.
88-- `gpu_util.json` is an array of `{t, util}` samples collected with `nvidia-smi` during the measured run. `t` is finite nonnegative elapsed seconds; `util` is a finite GPU utilisation percentage in [0,100]. The fixed sampler records the mean across GPUs returned by nvidia-smi, then the summarizer retains only samples during the shared command and rebases monotonic timestamps to its start. A sample with zero utilisation is valid. Empty arrays parse but fail the numeric gate; missing files or malformed samples fail parsing.
89-- The deterministic pipeline writes `A/profile-packet.json` with exact keys:
90-  - `stages`: the validated timing rows, preserving optional `kind`, each augmented with `wall_fraction = min(1, wall_s / total_wall_s)`, `start_s`, and `mean_gpu_util` (fraction in [0,1], or null). When supplied, `start_s` must be measured on the telemetry clock. Legacy rows without `start_s` record null start and utilisation; stage order does not establish a measured telemetry window. Stage endpoints must remain finite. Stage utilisation is the arithmetic mean of telemetry percentages divided by 100 in `[start_s, start_s + wall_s)`; no samples means null. Never substitute GPU busy seconds for utilisation;
91-  - `total_wall_s`: the measured total;
92-  - `timed_fraction = min(1, sum(stage.wall_s) / total_wall_s)`;
93-  - `gpu_telemetry`: true only when the validated `gpu_util.json` array is non-empty; stage `gpu_s` values do not establish telemetry.
94-  - `gpu_count`: `C/box.json.gpu_count` when nonnegative integer, otherwise count parsed from allocation `type` (`gpu_<N>x_...`), otherwise the collected probe's `nvidia.gpus.length`. Unavailable inventory defaults conservatively to 1; an empty inventory records 0.
95:  - `concurrency`: the validated `concurrency.json` object (see Concurrency probe), or null when the probe did not run or its output is missing or invalid.
96-  - `host_only`: boolean (U49). True exactly when the profile shows no CUDA activity: the rows `kernels`, `memcpy H2D`, `memcpy D2H` and `CUDA API host time` are all present, each with `wall_s` 0 and `gpu_s` 0 or null, and `gpu_util.json` holds at least one sample and every sample's `util` is 0. Otherwise false, including for profiles without those rows.
97-- Profile facts are `{profile_complete, timed_fraction, gpu_telemetry}` plus common `tokens_known` and `gpu_busy_known`, plus optional `headroom`: the packet's `concurrency.factor` (finite positive ratio) or null, and optional `host_only`: the packet's `host_only` boolean, or null when no packet was written. Every executed profile stage emits `headroom` and `host_only`; both are optional in the v2 schema so older records stay valid, and both are null on SKIPPED/stub records. `profile_complete` is true when the command exits 0 and all three inputs validate, even when the numeric gate fails. The deterministic gate requires at least three stages, no process wrappers, `timed_fraction >= 0.9`, and `gpu_telemetry=true`. A stage is a process wrapper if its name contains a case-insensitive token `process`, `wrapper`, `telemetry`, `total`, or `overall` delimited by whitespace, underscores, hyphens, or string boundaries, or if its `wall_s` is within 2% of `total_wall_s` (inclusive). Any wrapper fails the gate, even alongside three internal stages. In a host-only profile (packet `host_only` true) the `other host time` row is exempt from the 2% test, though not from the name test: the fixed profiler computes it as the wall-time remainder, so with no CUDA activity it is the whole command by construction rather than a wrapper around measured stages. Every other gate condition applies to host-only profiles unchanged, and profiles that are not host-only are gated exactly as before. A host-only profile leaves the pipelining and multi-GPU bounds at 1 (no transfer or compute time); its whole-workload bounds come only from the concurrency probe. Run evidence (blind-01 run9, replayed on its saved files 2026-11-01): the published baseline is CPU-only; Nsight recorded no CUDA kernel, memory or API activity, GPU utilisation was zero in every sample, and `other host time` was the whole command, so the 2% test failed the gate as `numeric` and the concurrency probe never ran. Owner decision 2026-11-01: CPU-only baselines are in scope. Numeric gate failures preserve the packet and use `error_class: numeric`; missing or invalid files use `error_class: parse`. A failed gate or parse stops downstream work without a profile repair.
98-
99-## Concurrency probe: calibration of same-GPU headroom
100-- Purpose: measure, before any prediction or method exists, how much more throughput one GPU gives when the unchanged published command runs several times at once. This measured factor is the only source of same-GPU headroom for bounds. No model call is involved.
101-- When the profile command exits 0 and the profile gate passes, the pipeline uploads trusted `m5/concurrency_probe.py` to remote `profiler/` and, through boxrun as operation `concurrency` with the resolved `profile` budget, runs `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py harness/run_command.sh out/concurrency <budget_s>` from the shared run directory. Remote `out/concurrency/` is cleared first. Fetched files land in `A/results/profile/out/concurrency/`; the log is `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. There is no agent repair and no execution retry. Probe receipts count toward profile v1 `usd` and `gpu_s` like other box receipts.
102-- Each invocation runs `bash harness/run_command.sh` with its working directory set to a fresh `concurrency-work/<label>/` under the shared run directory. That directory holds a symlink to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work` and `evaluation-work`, plus an empty `out/` directory. Labels are `single-1`, `single-2`, `single-3`, `n2-1`, `n2-2`, `n4-1` to `n4-4`. Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<label>.log` of the shared run directory. The environment is inherited unchanged apart from the MPS variables below. Nsight is not used.
103-- MPS: when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is on PATH, the probe starts a user-level daemon (`nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d`) with `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` and `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` set to fresh directories under `concurrency-work/`, passes both variables to every invocation, and stops the daemon (`echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with the same variables) before exiting, including after failures and on SIGTERM. If the daemon fails to start or any invocation fails under MPS, the probe stops the daemon, records `mps_failed: true`, and repeats the complete probe once without MPS in fresh work directories. Without the binary there is no MPS and `mps_failed` is false.
104:- MPS use is verified, not assumed. The daemon's `control.log` in its `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` records each client connection as a line containing `NEW CLIENT <pid> from user <uid>`. After each single run and each batch under MPS, the probe counts these lines (case-sensitive substring `NEW CLIENT `, followed by an integer pid and ` from user `). The count must have grown by at least the number of copies just run (1 for a single run, n for a batch of n). A missing or unreadable log, or a smaller increase, means the copies did not run under MPS: the probe treats this like an invocation failure under MPS (stop the daemon, `mps_failed: true`, repeat the complete probe once without MPS). `mps: true` is therefore recorded only when every counted measurement was verified to run under MPS. No log content enters `concurrency.json`.
105-- Sequence: three single runs one after another, then 2 copies started together, then 4 copies started together. Wall seconds come from a monotonic clock around each subprocess; a batch's wall runs from launching its first copy to the exit of its last. `T1` is the median of the single walls. A single run that exits nonzero stops the probe with a null factor. Before each batch, the batch is skipped when `n * T1` exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. A batch counts only when every copy exits 0. For a counted batch, `factor_n = n * T1 / wall_n`.
106:- `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mps, mps_failed, single_wall_s, batches, factor}`:
107-  - `mps`: boolean, true when the recorded measurements ran under MPS; `mps_failed`: boolean;
108-  - `single_wall_s`: array of exactly three entries, each a finite positive number or null (failed or not run);
109-  - `batches`: exactly two rows, in order n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`; `wall_s` and `factor` are finite positive numbers or null, `all_ok` and `skipped` are booleans, and `factor` is null unless the batch counted;
110-  - `factor`: the largest counted `factor_n`, or null when any single run failed or no batch counted.
111-  The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file, including with a null factor, and 2 when it cannot. It does not check output correctness: it measures throughput only.
112-- The probe never fails the profile stage and never changes the profile gate. A probe timeout, nonzero exit, or missing or invalid file gives packet `concurrency: null` and `headroom: null`. The pipeline validates the file against the exact shape above before copying it into the packet.
113:- Unit mode (U50). When the profile gate passes with packet `host_only` true and `A/harness/` holds both `run_units.sh` and `units.json`, the probe runs in unit mode: `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py --units harness/run_units.sh harness/units.json out/concurrency <budget_s>`, with the same upload, operation, budget, clearing, fetch, log location and no-retry rules as command mode. Otherwise the probe runs in command mode exactly as described above. Unit mode never uses MPS and does not look for the MPS binary. It compares the same four units run in one invocation, as separate invocations one after another, and as separate invocations at once, holding inputs and per-unit configuration fixed and checking every output byte for byte. Owner decision 2026-11-01: the smallest bounded experiment that resolves whether a CPU-only baseline's units gain throughput when run at once, with only the pipeline changes that comparison needs. Reader evidence (blind-01 run9): units are distinct inputs, selectable by restricting the prepared input list to original records (the command-line selector has no effect); each unit writes its own result files at the same paths in full and subset runs, with no run-specific content, and its outputs repeat bit for bit; the reproduce logs record every unit's cost; whether a unit reads state left by earlier units of the same invocation is unknown, which the comparison with the frozen baseline tests; units take 1 to 10 min with a cost spread over 50%; the baseline's own threads already use at least half the logical CPUs. Command mode would instead run three whole commands of 1 to 2 h and compare no outputs.
114-- Sample: units sorted by `cost_s` ascending, ties by manifest order; the sample is the four consecutive sorted units starting at sorted position floor((N - 4) / 2), N being the number of units, kept in that order as sample positions 0 to 3. Units near the median cost keep concurrent invocations of similar length, so a batch runs at its full width for nearly its whole wall time; the factor therefore describes typical units, not the shortest or longest.
115-- Arms run in this fixed order, every invocation in a fresh work directory built as in command mode (named `<label>` for an arm with one invocation, `<label>-<j>` for invocation j = 1, 2, ... of an arm with several):
116-  - `a-1`: one invocation `bash harness/run_units.sh <id0> <id1> <id2> <id3>` (sample order), the baseline's own serial mode;
117-  - `b-1`: four invocations of one unit each, one after another in sample order;
118-  - `c2-1`: sample units 0 and 1 started together, then, after both exit, units 2 and 3 started together;
119-  - `c4-1`: all four started together;
120-  - `c4-2`, `c2-2`, `b-2`, `a-2`: the same arms again in reverse order, to balance drift.
121-  Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<work directory name>.log` of the shared run directory, and its environment is inherited unchanged. An arm's wall runs on a monotonic clock from launching its first invocation to the exit of its last.
122-- Output checks. After `a-1`, every output path of every sample unit under `a-1`'s `out/` must be byte-identical to the same path under the shared run directory's `reproduce-out/` (`baseline_match`); a file missing on either side is a mismatch. When `a-1` exits nonzero or `baseline_match` is false, no later arm runs. After every later invocation, its units' output files must be byte-identical to `a-1`'s (`outputs_match`, true when every later executed invocation matched). An arm counts when all of its invocations exit 0 and all of their compared files match.
123-- Budget: before each arm, that arm and every later arm are skipped when its estimate exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. The estimate is the sum of the sample's `cost_s` for `a-1`, and `a-1`'s measured wall for every later arm.
124-- Resource use. For each invocation, from `os.wait4` on its process (which includes its waited-for descendants): `cpu_s` (user plus system seconds), `max_rss_kb`, `nivcsw` (involuntary context switches), `inblock` and `oublock`. For each arm, sampled about once a second while it runs: `busy_fraction` (mean non-idle share of total CPU time from `/proc/stat`, idle including iowait), `mem_available_min_kb` (the minimum `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo`) and `threads_max` (the largest sum of `Threads` from `/proc/<pid>/status` over the processes of the arm's invocations; each invocation starts its own session and process group). An arm's `cpu_s` is the sum over its invocations and `effective_cores` is that sum divided by the arm's wall. Memory bandwidth and caches are not measured.
125:- In unit mode `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mode, mps, mps_failed, outcome, units_total, sample, baseline_match, outputs_match, serial_wall_s, separate_wall_s, batches, arms, nproc, mem_total_kb, factor}`:
126-  - `mode`: `"units"`; `mps` and `mps_failed`: false;
127-  - `outcome`: the first that applies of `"invalid_units"` (manifest unreadable, invalid or with fewer than four units), `"failed"` (an executed invocation exited nonzero), `"baseline_mismatch"`, `"outputs_mismatch"`, `"skipped"` (no `c2` or `c4` arm counted), otherwise `"measured"`;
128-  - `units_total`: N, or null for `invalid_units`; `sample`: four rows `{index, cost_s}` in sample order, `index` being the manifest position, or `[]` for `invalid_units`. No unit identifier or output path appears in the file;
129-  - `baseline_match` and `outputs_match`: booleans, or null when not evaluated;
130-  - `serial_wall_s`: the mean wall of the counted `a` arms; `separate_wall_s`: the mean wall of the counted `b` arms; each a finite positive number or null;
131-  - `batches`: exactly two rows, n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`: `wall_s` is the mean wall of the executed `c<n>` arms or null when none ran, `skipped` is true when none ran, `all_ok` is true when at least one ran and every executed one counted, and `factor` is `serial_wall_s / wall_s` when `all_ok` is true and `outcome` is `measured`, otherwise null;
132-  - `arms`: exactly eight rows in the fixed order, each exactly `{label, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, cpu_s, effective_cores, busy_fraction, mem_available_min_kb, threads_max, invocations}`, with `label` from `a-1` to `a-2`; numbers are finite and nonnegative, or null when the arm did not run; `invocations` lists the executed invocations in launch order, each exactly `{units, rc, wall_s, cpu_s, max_rss_kb, nivcsw, inblock, oublock}`, `units` being sample positions;
133-  - `nproc`: `os.cpu_count()`; `mem_total_kb`: `MemTotal` from `/proc/meminfo`;
134-  - `factor`: the largest non-null batch factor, or null.
135-  The factor compares the baseline's own serial mode with concurrent invocations over the same units, so per-invocation start-up costs count against it; `separate_wall_s` minus `serial_wall_s` shows that cost. The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file and 2 when it cannot.
136-- The pipeline validates a unit-mode file against the exact shape above, including each batch factor and `factor` as the largest batch factor, before copying it into the packet; anything else gives `concurrency: null`. Bounds and propose read only `factor`, `mps` and `mps_failed`, so they treat a unit-mode factor like a command-mode one, and a measured unit-mode factor below 1.05 is a valid negative finding (`mps` and `mps_failed` both false).

138-## C/receipts/ and stage failure signatures
139-- Every box command (uploads, probe, setup attempts, anchor execution, profiling, implementation) runs through `m5/boxrun.sh`; every receipt is `C/receipts/NNNN-<operation>.json`. Operations are `upload`, `probe`, `setup`, `anchors`, `profile`, `concurrency`, `implement-baseline`, `adapter-smoke`, `implement-state`, `implement-upload`, `implement-patch`, `setup-method`, `run-method`, `run-tests`; numbering continues across existing receipts. Receipt/log IDs contain no benchmark labels.
140-- Receipts use the boxrun format: `{name, rc, timed_out, wall_s, budget_s, overrun, fetched, started_utc, ended_utc, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known}`. `name` is the receipt ID; `rc` is an integer remote exit code or null; `timed_out` and `fetched` are booleans; `wall_s` is nonnegative integer elapsed seconds; `budget_s` is the positive integer timeout supplied to boxrun; `overrun` is boolean, true on timeout or when measured wall_s exceeds budget_s; timestamps are UTC strings. Remote `out/` is fetched using the unchanged boxrun interface. After the remote command finishes, boxrun fetches remote `out/` and then the operation log; a fetch that fails is retried up to four more times, waiting 60 s before each retry (environment `BOXRUN_FETCH_WAIT_S` overrides the wait, for tests), and `fetched` is true only when both fetches succeed. A retry repeats only the fetch, never the remote command. Retry waits count in `wall_s`. Receipt contents stay in control; runtime logs stay in agent results.
141-- Failed reproduce/profile signatures have fixed `error_class`: `infra` for unavailable box execution/receipts, failed upload, or failed fetch after a successful command, or a fixed profiler infrastructure marker; `install` for failed setup after the bounded repairs; `anchor` for an anchor-run failure or a failed anchor; `parse` for missing/invalid output files, unavailable harness files, or a nonzero profile command exit; `numeric` for a parsed profile that fails the stage-count, process-wrapper, coverage, or GPU telemetry gate. Exit codes are 4 for anchor failures, 3 for timeouts and 2 for the other failures. `infra` is added to the shared v1 error-class enum so the v2 envelope remains v1-valid. Box/fetch stdout and stderr are never copied into operator signatures.
142-- Any box receipt with rc=124 or timed_out=true records a timeout, even when fetch fails. A final timeout fails its stage with `error_class: timeout`, exit 3. Authored setup and anchor scripts consume their existing repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors), and method/test scripts their one bounded repair; method/test timeout repairs expose only the fixed timeout count plus budget/elapsed/overrun seconds, never test content. Transport, patch, probe, integrity and immutable evaluator commands permit one identical retry under the same budget (under keys `setup`, `anchors` and `profile`, the budget resolved at the retry's start, U47), without editing scientific payloads or trusted scorers. A second timeout stops that operation and stage. The fixed profiler permits no repair or execution retry; its first timeout stops profiling with `error_class: timeout`.
143-- Reproduce, profile, implement and evaluate facts optionally add exactly typed timeout fields `{timed_out: boolean, budget_s: nonnegative integer, overrun: boolean}` when a box timeout occurs. `timed_out=true` records any attempt timing out, `budget_s` is the latest timed-out command's budget, and `overrun` is true when any timed-out receipt overruns. These fields survive a successful bounded repair; stage status then reflects the repaired result. Older records and SKIPPED/stub records retain their existing fact keys. No command output or new free-text fields enter signatures.
144-- Numeric ratio facts accept finite JSON numbers, including integer spellings such as `0` and `1`; booleans remain invalid. This permits fully timed profiles to emit the capped fraction `1`.
145-- Every stage records its own elapsed wall-clock seconds in v1 `wall_s`, excluding signature emission. SKIPPED stages measure only their skip handling, never the prior stage's duration.
146-- Runner results add boolean `tokens_known`, true when the provider reports input/output usage (including reported zeros). wf exposes `agent.usage()` as a cumulative snapshot `{calls, tokens_in, tokens_out, unknown}`; `unknown` counts runner attempts without usage. Repairs, failed attempts, shadow calls, and fallbacks all contribute; cached calls do not incur usage. Compatible runners without `tokens_known` are accepted when their input/output counts are integers.
147-- Stages aggregate reported input/output counts into v1 `tokens_in`/`tokens_out`; `facts.tokens_known` is true only when every runner attempt in that stage reports usage. With no attempts, existing unknown/null facts remain unchanged. Unknown counts retain numeric zero placeholders required by v1. `gpu_busy_known` reflects box receipt telemetry for reproduce/profile (see Compute metadata); harness profile evidence is reported separately. Downstream scientific stages are skipped after either failed gate; takeaways still runs.

149-## A/bounds.json (computed before the seal agent)
150-- `python3 m5/bounds.py <profile-packet.json> <out.json>` writes an atomic JSON object keyed by the five menu methods. Each value is `{p, k, bound, feasible, k_derivation, stages}`. `stages` contains actionable rows `{stage, kind, wall_fraction, mean_gpu_util, methods}`; `methods` lists every menu method that acts on that stage: whole-workload methods act on every stage, the others on stages of their kind. Exit 0 means success; exit 1 means invalid/missing input or unavailable output, with content-free diagnostics. Legacy packets without `gpu_count` default to 1. GPU counts must be nonnegative integers.
151-- Explicit stage `kind` takes precedence. Without it, lowercase stage names are split into ASCII alphanumeric tokens. Any token `transfer`, `transfers`, `h2d`, `d2h`, `htod`, `dtoh`, `copy`, `memcpy`, `upload`, or `download` means transfer; otherwise any token `compute`, `kernel`, `kernels`, `inference`, `training`, `forward`, or `backward` means compute. All other names mean other. Other stages and unmeasured time remain serial.
152-- The fixed mapping and maximum factors are:
153-
154-  | Method | Acts on | p | Maximum factor k | bound |
155-  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
156-  | data-parallel over inputs | whole workload | 1 | min(8, factor) | k |
157-  | ensembles | whole workload | 1 | min(8, factor) | k |
158-  | batching | whole workload | 1 | min(4, factor) | k |
159-  | pipelining | transfer stages | transfer fraction | 2 | Amdahl |
160-  | multi-GPU | compute stages | compute fraction | max(1, gpu_count) | Amdahl / k |
161-
162-- `factor` is the packet's `concurrency.factor`: the same-GPU concurrent throughput measured during calibration (see Concurrency probe). When the packet has no `concurrency` key, `concurrency` is null, or its factor is null or below 1, whole-workload methods use `k=1` (bound 1, infeasible): missing measurements never manufacture headroom. A `concurrency` value that is neither null nor an object, or a factor that is neither null nor a finite number, fails parsing.
163-- `Amdahl = 1 / ((1-p) + p/k)` with `p = min(1, sum(actionable stage.wall_s) / total_wall_s)`. Fractions are recomputed from timings, never trusted from supplied `wall_fraction`. The multi-GPU bound is speedup per GPU-second, `Amdahl / k`: the same equal-cost basis that evaluation applies (`cost_ratio <= 1`) against a one-GPU baseline. It exceeds 1 only with superlinear evidence, which Amdahl cannot supply. Zero GPUs uses `k=1`.
164-- `k_derivation`: whole-workload methods record `{rule:"min(fixed_cap, concurrency factor)", fixed_cap, factor, mps}` (`factor` and `mps` null when unavailable); pipelining records `{rule:"fixed_cap", fixed_cap:2}`; multi-GPU records `{rule:"max(1, gpu_count)", gpu_count, amdahl, cost_basis:"equal_gpu_seconds"}`. Stage `mean_gpu_util` is carried for information only and never sets a factor.
165-- These are ceilings for sealed intervals, not measured method improvements. The concurrency factor is the measured throughput of plain concurrent runs; method code may exceed it in evaluation, but sealed intervals may not. `feasible` is true exactly when `bound >= 1.05`.
166-- The seal and propose prompts describe the bounds this way: whole-workload bounds are measured concurrent throughput on one GPU; pipelining is Amdahl over transfer time; multi-GPU bounds are per GPU-second at equal cost.
167-- The pipeline regenerates `A/bounds.json` before sealing, reads it before the agent call, and supplies its path and contents in the seal prompt. Missing or invalid profile evidence fails sealing; stale bounds cannot substitute for it.

169-## A/PREDICTIONS.json (written by the seal agent; checked, then sealed)
170-- `predictions`: an array, one item per feasible method, with unique methods taken from the menu ["data-parallel over inputs", "batching", "multi-GPU", "ensembles", "pipelining"]. Each item has:
171-  - `expected_speedup_interval` with finite numbers satisfying `low > 0`, `low <= high <= bound`, and width `high-low <= bound-1` for that method;
172-  - `outcome_vs_compute_points`, holding for every value in compute_budgets one {compute_budget, predicted_outcome, uncertainty}, all non-empty. `predicted_outcome` and `uncertainty` must not be null, empty strings, or empty objects/arrays. When no numeric forecast is supported, use an explicit non-empty declaration such as `predicted_outcome={not_applicable:true,reason:"fixed-work benchmark; no calibrated outcome curve"}` and explain unavailable evidence in `uncertainty`. Do not invent a number. `equal_outcome_target.not_applicable` does not waive these point fields.
173-- `outputs_stochastic` is a required boolean. It is true for Monte Carlo, sampling, or outputs affected by random seeds, including reproducible fixed-seed runs.
174-- Stochastic seals require statistical `equivalence_metrics` with positive absolute margins and non-empty names/sources, `paired_seed_tests.kind="paired_median"` with unique integer seeds, and `confidence_rule.equivalence={kind:"paired_median",confidence}` with finite confidence in [0.5,1). The sealed significance level is `1-confidence`. Margins come from scientific requirements or baseline variability (for example Monte Carlo standard error); paired-difference confidence intervals must lie within the sealed margins. Exact/bitwise rules, zero margins, relative margins, deterministic seed declarations, and prose-only rules are rejected for stochastic outputs. The check reads executable fields only: evaluation applies each metric's `name` and numeric `tolerance`, so an exact or bitwise rule is a zero or missing absolute margin. Free-text metric fields (`comparison`, `kind`, `rule` and any others) are never scanned for words; statistical terms such as "exact binomial bound" are allowed. Exact or bitwise rules apply only to deterministic outputs.
175-- The seal agent reads `A/intake/`, `A/profile-packet.json`, `A/bounds.json` and the baseline's measured outputs under `A/results/reproduce/` (the fetched `out/`, logs and `anchors_scored.json`), and nothing else. A margin derived from baseline variability names, in its `source`, the measured file and the statistic used (for example the standard deviation of a per-seed outcome across the baseline's seeds). When neither a scientific requirement nor measured baseline variability supports a positive margin, the seal agent never invents one, and the seal fails `stochastic_equivalence_invalid` as before. The seal prompt states all three.
176-- Required non-empty keys: equivalence_metrics, paired_seed_tests, sample_sizes, confidence_rule, hardware_cost_basis, timing_scope, minimum_worthwhile_gain (a number > 1), evaluation_inputs, splits, compute_budgets (at least 3 distinct positive numbers), repetitions (an integer >= 5), warmup, scheduling_order, equal_outcome_target and baseline_invocation_s.
177-- `baseline_invocation_s` is `{seconds, source}`. `seconds` is a finite positive number: the expected process wall, from launch to exit, of one complete baseline equivalence invocation over all sealed seeds and inputs (what the implement adapter smoke measures), derived from the reproduce measurements. `source` is a non-empty string naming the measured file, the measured value and the arithmetic (for example two sequential eight-replica ensembles at the measured ensemble wall, plus process start-up). Any other shape is `protocol_incomplete`. The seal check projects one complete performance scorer at that estimate, with the adapter smoke's rule: `projected_s` = (`warmup` + `repetitions`) × 2 × `seconds`, plus, unless `equal_outcome_target.not_applicable` is true, `b / baseline_gpus + b / method_gpus` for each compute budget `b` (GPU counts from `hardware_cost_basis`). When at least one method is feasible and `projected_s` exceeds 0.9 × the resolved `evaluate` budget, the seal fails `protocol_cost`; a seal with no feasible method skips this check. The seal prompt states the resolved `evaluate` budget in seconds, this projection and the 0.9 factor, and says that `seconds` comes from the measurements and is never lowered to fit: the protocol fits through its choice of seeds, inputs, warmup, repetitions and compute budgets. The adapter smoke still measures the real cost.
178-- `infeasible_methods` is a required array of `{method, reason}`, exactly once for every method with `bound < 1.05`; reasons are non-empty strings. These methods must never appear in predictions. Every feasible method must appear exactly once in predictions and never in infeasible_methods. With at least two feasible methods, all prediction intervals must not be identical. One feasible method is exempt from this comparison.
179-- Seal failures use `error_class: numeric` (exit 2), including invalid protocol, invalid intervals, missing/duplicate method coverage, or unavailable bounds. Facts retain exactly `seal_present`, `seal_verified`, `prediction_count` plus common facts; `prediction_count` counts submitted prediction rows, excluding infeasible entries. An empty feasible menu may be sealed as a negative result: a verified seal with zero predictions (every menu method listed in `infeasible_methods`) PASSes the seal stage with `prediction_count=0` and `reason_codes: []`. Propose then decides whether the absence is a negative finding or missing measurements.
180-- The seal prompt embeds stochastic and deterministic JSON skeletons generated by `m5/seal_protocol.js`, using the same constants as its deterministic validation. Both specify `equivalence_metrics=[{name,source,tolerance:{abs:number}}]` with non-empty **string** names and sources, never citation objects. The stochastic example uses `paired_seed_tests={kind:"paired_median",seeds:[0,1,2,3,4,5]}` and a positive absolute margin; the deterministic example uses `{kind:"deterministic",justification:"scientific reason"}` and zero absolute tolerance. Both include `evaluation_inputs={ids:["held-out-1"]}`, matching `sample_sizes={inputs:1,seeds:6}` (stochastic) or `{inputs:1,seeds:1}` (deterministic), `confidence_rule={performance:{kind:"paired_median",confidence:0.95},equivalence:{kind:"paired_median",confidence:0.95}}`, and `baseline_invocation_s={seconds:<placeholder number>,source:"<placeholder>"}`. Example metric names, sources, margins, identities and justifications must be replaced with supported scientific choices. Six seeds give finite two-sided 95% bounds for one metric; more metrics or higher confidence can require more seeds. Deterministic evaluation uses one null seed.
181-- One bounded repair is allowed for a readable but invalid protocol or a missing/malformed predictions file, before any immutable seal files are written. Initial `seal` and optional `seal-repair` calls use `ls-writer`, requested model `sonnet`, `repairable:false`, `fresh:true`; runner-level repair is disabled. The repair prompt supplies only script-owned failing reason codes and field paths as validation feedback, without values, evidence, bounds, measurements, exception text or model commentary. The agent may read and rewrite only `A/PREDICTIONS.json`, preserving scientific intent without inventing evidence or loosening tolerances. The complete deterministic checks run again exactly once; failure stops, success proceeds to the existing seal writer. Bounds generation, agent execution, seal storage/verification failures and verified negative results do not trigger repair. Repair never allocates a seal number or modifies prior receipts/frozen predictions. No field paths or feedback enter operator signatures. For `protocol_cost` the field paths are `warmup`, `repetitions`, `paired_seed_tests.seeds`, `evaluation_inputs.ids`, `compute_budgets` and `baseline_invocation_s`, and the repair prompt also restates the resolved `evaluate` budget in seconds and the projection rule from the seal prompt; it supplies no other value.
182-- `C/stages/seal.json` adds `reason_codes`, an array containing the final failed check's fixed code, or `[]` for PASS, SKIPPED, and stub results. Checks stop at the first failure, in the order below. Exceptions use the code for the operation/check in progress. Codes are script-owned literals; no agent text, exception messages, methods, paths, or scientific content enter this field. Existing numeric error class, exit code, signature facts, and immutable seal receipt format are unchanged.

202-## Propose, independent votes, and the one-shot gate
203-- Before reading profile/bounds or calling any agent, propose selects the highest-numbered `C/seals/NNNN.json` and hashes the exact bytes of both `A/PREDICTIONS.json` and the receipt's frozen `path`. Both must match `sha256`. A missing, unreadable, or mismatched seal fails with `error_class: other` (exit 2), with no model calls.
204-- The deterministic step reads `A/profile-packet.json`, `A/bounds.json`, and the verified predictions. Feasible predicted methods have `bounds[method].feasible=true` and `bound >= 1.05`. Their ranking score is `min(low/2 + high/2, bound)`, descending; ties follow the fixed menu order. Unknown/duplicate methods or malformed intervals fail parsing.
205-- Resource guards use `C/box.json.gpu_count` when supplied (a nonnegative integer), otherwise the count in allocation `type` such as `gpu_1x_a10`. Probe capacity is `A/results/probe/probe.json.nvidia.gpus.length`. Available GPUs are the smaller count; either inventory unavailable means no method passes. Ordinary methods require one GPU; multi-GPU requires `max(2, bounds[method].k)` GPUs, matching the factor used for its bound. Methods failing these guards are excluded from selection.
206-- `A/propose-packet.json` contains only `{ranked_methods, stage_to_method, bounds, sealed_equivalence_rule}`. Ranked rows are `{method,bounds}` in deterministic ranking order, restricted to feasible resource-safe methods. `stage_to_method` contains every stage as `{stage,wall_fraction,mean_gpu_util,methods}`; other stages map to an empty method list. `bounds` contains all five bounds and their `k_derivation` and actionable stages. `sealed_equivalence_rule` contains only `outputs_stochastic`, `equivalence_metrics`, `paired_seed_tests`, `sample_sizes`, and the equivalence portion of `confidence_rule`. No raw profile, predicted outcome curves, intake, resource inventory, performance protocol, or other content enters the packet. Prompts state that ranked methods already passed deterministic GPU resource guards. Proposer and all five skeptics receive the identical packet; skeptics additionally receive the validated proposal. When no feasible resource-safe method remains (including a verified seal with zero predictions), propose makes no model calls, writes `A/propose-packet.json` and `A/GATE.json` as usual, and keeps `method="none"`, `expected_speedup=null` and `gate_pass=false`. The absence is a negative finding exactly when it rests on measurements: the profile packet's `concurrency.factor` is a finite number; its MPS state is verified, meaning `concurrency.mps` is true, or `concurrency.mps` and `concurrency.mps_failed` are both false (MPS absent from the box); and both GPU inventories used by the resource guards (box and probe) are available with at least one GPU each. Then the stage PASSes with `outcome="no_feasible_method"`; implement and evaluate are SKIPPED with null facts, takeaways runs, and the run's stop point is propose. Otherwise (concurrency missing, null or not finite; `concurrency.mps_failed` true, meaning MPS exists on the box but the measurement could not use it; or either GPU inventory unavailable or reporting zero GPUs) the absence reflects missing measurements: the stage FAILs with `numeric` (exit 2) as before and `outcome` stays null. The finding is bounded: no method on the fixed menu has measured headroom of at least 1.05 on this hardware (concurrency factor of plain concurrent copies, GPU count, measured transfer share). It does not show that no method could speed up the workload.
207-- One `propose` call (`ls-writer`, requested model `sonnet`) reads only the embedded packet and writes `A/proposal.json`, with exactly `{method, rationale, plan_steps, files_expected, risks}`. `method` must be in the ranked list; `rationale` is a non-empty string; the remaining fields are arrays of non-empty strings. `plan_steps` and `files_expected` must be non-empty; `risks` may be empty. The call cannot implement code or access the box. Invalid/missing proposals fail with `error_class: parse` (exit 2).
208-- Five concurrent skeptic calls (`qt-bare`, requested model `haiku`, mapping to the cheap tier) each start a fresh session. Ballot `i` uses label `skeptic-<i>`, so names are `x-<raid>-skeptic-1` through `x-<raid>-skeptic-5` with no sibling suffix. Each receives the same prepared packet and validated proposal, plus its ballot number, and no other votes. Model family/endpoint selection remains with the workflow configuration (see m5 model policy); the pipeline pins no endpoint.
209-- Ballots have exactly `{vote, reason_codes}`. `vote` is `approve`, `reject`, or `abstain`; `reason_codes` is an array (possibly empty) containing only `exceeds_bound`, `not_parallelisable`, `changes_method`, `equivalence_risk`, `resource_mismatch`, `weak_profile_evidence`, or `other`. The pipeline writes `A/votes/1.json` through `5.json`; missing/failed/invalid responses are written as JSON `null` (null ballots). No vote repair or replacement is allowed.
210-- Ballot meanings. `reject` names a defect that would make the proposed method fail as planned: it exceeds its bound, cannot be parallelised as planned, changes the sealed method, risks breaking the sealed equivalence rule, or mismatches the resources (codes `exceeds_bound`, `not_parallelisable`, `changes_method`, `equivalence_risk`, `resource_mismatch`, or `other`). `abstain` means the packet is insufficient to judge (typically `weak_profile_evidence`); it is not a judgement against the method. `approve` means no defect is found and the evidence is adequate. The skeptic prompt states these three meanings and that missing or weak evidence warrants abstain, not reject. The gate counts only the `vote` field; reason codes never reclassify a ballot. Skeptic review records evidence about the proposal; a vote count is not scientific ground truth, and execution plus independent evaluation decide the claim.
211-- These calls use wf option `repairable:false`: no repair turn, schema/no-JSON failures cannot trigger fallback, panels are bypassed, and shadow mode becomes fallback. Transport failures can still use the configured family chain. This preserves existing default behavior for other calls. `fresh:true` bypasses the resume cache for proposer and skeptics; every ballot starts a new runner session.
212-- `A/GATE.json` records the propose facts. Its presence prevents another proposal/vote round in the same run (fails with `other`). Gate requires at most one ballot that is a rejection or null (abstentions never count against the gate, and no minimum number of approvals applies), the selected sealed interval's `high >= minimum_worthwhile_gain`, `high <= bound`, and passing resource guards. Gate failures use `numeric` (exit 2); malformed inputs use `parse`. Downstream stages skip after failure; takeaways still runs.
213-- Facts have exactly `{method, expected_speedup, votes_approve, votes_total, vote_share, gate_pass}` plus common `tokens_known` and `gpu_busy_known`. `method` is a menu entry or `none`; `expected_speedup` is the selected sealed interval midpoint, or null before selection. Executed stages initialize `votes_approve=0`, `votes_total=5`, `vote_share=0`, and `gate_pass=false`; `vote_share=votes_approve/5`. Missing votes never reduce the denominator. vote_share is diagnostic only. SKIPPED/stub stages retain the existing null facts contract. Scientific text and reason codes remain in the agent view.
214-- Propose facts add optional `votes_reject` and `votes_abstain` (nonnegative integers) and `outcome` (`"approved"`, `"rejected"`, `"conditions_unmet"`, `"no_feasible_method"`, or null). They are optional in the v2 schema so older records stay valid; every executed propose stage emits all three, initialised to 0, 0 and null, and SKIPPED/stub records hold null. Null ballots number `5 - votes_approve - votes_reject - votes_abstain`. Once ballots are counted: `outcome="approved"` exactly when the gate passes; `"rejected"` when two or more ballots are rejections or null; `"conditions_unmet"` when the ballot condition holds but an interval or resource condition fails. `"no_feasible_method"` is set only by the measured negative finding above, with all ballot counts 0. `outcome` stays null when the stage stops before ballots are counted for any other reason (seal, packet, proposal or parse failures, no feasible method without measurements, or an existing `A/GATE.json`). `OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` shows `outcome` and the four ballot counts (approve, reject, abstain, null) in the propose row. Its null-ballot count is `5 - votes_approve - votes_reject - votes_abstain` only when ballots were counted (outcome `approved`, `rejected` or `conditions_unmet`); otherwise it shows null, because no ballot was requested. When propose has `outcome="no_feasible_method"`, it also adds the fixed line `Finding: negative. No menu method has measured headroom of at least 1.05 on this hardware.`; it adds no such line otherwise.
215-
216-## Implement, frozen independent tests, and launch review
217-- `implement` verifies the latest seal against both prediction copies before doing work, and checks that the proposal selects a sealed method with equivalence metrics and a paired-seed protocol. It rechecks the seal before authoring, each attempt, and after review. A new latest seal, even with identical prediction bytes, invalidates the in-progress implementation. Existing `C/implement/`, `A/tests/`, `A/method/`, or `A/REVIEW.json` prevents restarting this stage and resetting its repair budget. Explicit `args.stub.implement` retains the existing stub contract.
218-- The pipeline first snapshots the already-built remote `baseline-published/`, `data/`, and a copy of the frozen baseline outputs, remote `reproduce-out/`, at `baseline-out/` (never the current `out/`). A missing or symlinked `reproduce-out/` fails the snapshot like any other snapshot failure. It does not rebuild or substitute the published baseline. All snapshots and subsequent integrity checks run through boxrun. Source, data, and baseline-output hashes must remain unchanged after authoring and around both attempts.
219-- Baseline adapter smoke: after the snapshot and before the test author call, implement runs the baseline adapter evaluate will use (`harness/run_evaluation.sh`, or `harness/run_anchors.sh` when absent) once, as box operation `adapter-smoke` under the method_run budget. It runs exactly as an evaluate invocation in a fresh `evaluation-work/smoke/0/baseline/`, with `EVAL_ARM=baseline`, `EVAL_MODE=equivalence`, the sealed `EVAL_PROTOCOL` and `EVAL_INPUTS`, empty `EVAL_COMPUTE_BUDGET`, and `EVAL_SEEDS` equal to the sealed `paired_seed_tests` object unchanged. Evaluate never passes a subset of the sealed seeds, so the smoke does not either: it is one complete baseline equivalence invocation. The smoke passes when the command exits 0 and `EVAL_OUT/evaluation.json` meets the evaluation record rules: one record per sealed seed and input id, seeds first, then input ids, in sealed order (seed null under a deterministic seal); the sealed `timing_scope`; the sealed `gpu_count`; finite positive `wall_s` for reported timing; and every sealed `equivalence_metrics` name in each record's `metrics` as a finite number. The smoke also checks its cost. Remote `out/smoke.json` is removed before each smoke; the smoke script times the adapter command with a monotonic clock from launch to exit and always writes `out/smoke.json` as exactly `{"process_wall_s": <finite nonnegative number>}`, including after a nonzero exit or TERM. When the records and metrics pass, implement projects one complete performance scorer from that measurement: `projected_s` = (sealed `warmup` + sealed `repetitions`) × 2 × `process_wall_s`, charging the method arm at the baseline's cost, plus, unless `equal_outcome_target.not_applicable` is true, `b / baseline_gpus + b / method_gpus` for each sealed compute budget `b` (each curve invocation's bound, with the GPU counts from `hardware_cost_basis`). The smoke passes only when `projected_s` is at most 0.9 × the resolved `evaluate` budget; otherwise it fails with category `cost`. A missing or malformed `smoke.json` after the records and metrics pass is category `missing_output`. On failure, one `adapter-repair` call (`harness` role and model, `retry: 1`, fresh session) may rewrite only `run_evaluation.sh` (creating it when absent). It receives the sealed predictions, intake files, current harness scripts, the fixed failure category (`exit`, `timeout`, `missing_output`, `records`, `metrics`, `cost`) and at most the last 200 log lines; for `cost` it also receives `process_wall_s`, the sealed warmup and repetitions, `projected_s` and the evaluate budget seconds, as numbers; its prompt states the evaluation adapter interface. Rewrites of any other file are discarded, as in reproduce repairs; a repair that leaves no nonempty `run_evaluation.sh` passing `bash -n` counts as a second failure. The rewritten script is copied to `A/harness/`, uploaded as `implement-upload`, and smoked once more. A second failure stops implement before any test or method author call: status `VOID`, `error_class: parse` (exit 2), or `timeout` (exit 3) when that smoke timed out, with `patch_applies`, `tests_pass`, `blind_tests` and `launch_review_pass` null. Smoke logs and outputs go to `A/results/implement/adapter/<attempt>/`; they are not measurements and evaluate never reads them. Test and method authors see the harness after any repair.
220-- There is one initial `tests` call and one initial `implement` call, both `ls-writer`, requested model `sonnet`, `repairable:false`, `fresh:true`. Tests are authored and frozen **before** the method-author call, so method results cannot precede the freeze. The test author receives only proposal, intake, baseline harness/interface and reproduced baseline outputs, and the sealed predictions/protocol. The method author receives proposal, intake, baseline harness, box probe and sealed predictions, and in its prompt the frozen `method_outputs` paths (see A/tests/); it never receives the tests' other content, fixtures or test transcripts. Only the initial method-author call may access the already-running box through `~/.cache/metis-serve/box.sh`.
221-- wf's optional agent setting `isolation` has `{directory, hidden, box_access}`: an absolute private view directory, an array of absolute paths hidden from that role, and a boolean permitting box credentials. It overrides cwd and add-dirs, disables resume-cache reuse and provider-session export, and is forwarded to every dispatched family, including fallbacks. Real dispatch uses bubblewrap with a read-only host filesystem, private `/tmp`, PID/IPC namespaces, hidden run/workflow paths and provider histories, and a fresh writable HOME containing authentication files only. The view is the only writable host directory. The initial implementer additionally receives read-only access to the existing box wrapper and SSH keys. Test, review and repair roles cannot access them. No sandbox fallback grants broader access: missing bubblewrap or unavailable namespaces fails the call. That outer namespace is the only sandbox: hosts that restrict unprivileged user namespaces (Ubuntu's AppArmor `bwrap-userns-restrict`) deny any namespace nested inside it, so a provider's own sandbox would fail every command. Inside the namespace a Codex agent therefore runs with `danger-full-access`, never `workspace-write` or `read-only`. That mode follows only from the call being dispatched inside the namespace, never from an environment variable: a Codex call outside isolation keeps `workspace-write` or `read-only` even when `CODEX_EPHEMERAL=1` is set. A role whose tools include Write, Edit or Bash keeps the view writable; any other role gets the view mounted read-only, with only its private HOME and temporary directory writable. `WF_STUB` remains an explicit test double, bypassing provider execution. Temporary views/provider state are removed after the stage; raw provider logs remain under the role's workflow transcript directory and are hidden from other roles.
222-- Each view has top-level `proposal.json`, `PREDICTIONS.json`, `intake/`, and `harness/`. Test views additionally have `baseline-out/`, a copy of `A/results/reproduce/out/`, so frozen tests run against the same baseline outputs their author saw; method views have `probe.json` and, on repair, the previous three method files. Writable author output is `tests/` or `method/`. Review views contain `method/`, proposal, predictions, intake, `implement-payload.json` and `seal.json`; `seal.json` is the existing seal receipt plus `receipt`, its numbered receipt filename. Review receives these scientific inputs embedded in its prompt, using the tool-free `qt-bare` role. No view contains another role's source or transcripts except the method source explicitly supplied to review.
223-
224-### A/method/ and remote execution interface
225-- The method author writes three required nonempty files: `method.patch` (git-style paths relative to the published source root), `setup_method.sh`, and `run_method.sh`. An optional fourth file, `run_anchors.sh`, implements the method anchor protocol. No other files are allowed. Shell scripts must pass `bash -n`. The pipeline copies them from the private view into `A/method/`; neither author writes control state.

An absent, empty or whitespace-only file without that statement for its own activity, and any other missing or malformed report, still fails parsing. Run evidence (blind-01 run9, 2026-11-01): the baseline ran to completion under the profiler with no CUDA activity and no capture problem; Nsight 2025 logged the three skips and wrote three empty summary files, and the summariser failed on a missing CSV header, so profile stopped with `parse` instead of reaching its numeric gate. Aggregate CSV reports do not identify critical-path intervals: if the four reported sums exceed measured wall, their wall allocations are scaled proportionally to fit. 95:  - `concurrency`: the validated `concurrency.json` object (see Concurrency probe), or null when the probe did not run or its output is missing or invalid.
103:- MPS: when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is on PATH, the probe starts a user-level daemon (`nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d`) with `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` and `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` set to fresh directories under `concurrency-work/`, passes both variables to every invocation, and stops the daemon (`echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with the same variables) before exiting, including after failures and on SIGTERM. If the daemon fails to start or any invocation fails under MPS, the probe stops the daemon, records `mps_failed: true`, and repeats the complete probe once without MPS in fresh work directories. Without the binary there is no MPS and `mps_failed` is false.
104:- MPS use is verified, not assumed. The daemon's `control.log` in its `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` records each client connection as a line containing `NEW CLIENT <pid> from user <uid>`. After each single run and each batch under MPS, the probe counts these lines (case-sensitive substring `NEW CLIENT `, followed by an integer pid and ` from user `). The count must have grown by at least the number of copies just run (1 for a single run, n for a batch of n). A missing or unreadable log, or a smaller increase, means the copies did not run under MPS: the probe treats this like an invocation failure under MPS (stop the daemon, `mps_failed: true`, repeat the complete probe once without MPS). `mps: true` is therefore recorded only when every counted measurement was verified to run under MPS. No log content enters `concurrency.json`.
106:- `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mps, mps_failed, single_wall_s, batches, factor}`:
111:  The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file, including with a null factor, and 2 when it cannot. It does not check output correctness: it measures throughput only.
113:- Unit mode (U50). When the profile gate passes with packet `host_only` true and `A/harness/` holds both `run_units.sh` and `units.json`, the probe runs in unit mode: `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py --units harness/run_units.sh harness/units.json out/concurrency <budget_s>`, with the same upload, operation, budget, clearing, fetch, log location and no-retry rules as command mode. Otherwise the probe runs in command mode exactly as described above. Unit mode never uses MPS and does not look for the MPS binary. It compares the same four units run in one invocation, as separate invocations one after another, and as separate invocations at once, holding inputs and per-unit configuration fixed and checking every output byte for byte. Owner decision 2026-11-01: the smallest bounded experiment that resolves whether a CPU-only baseline's units gain throughput when run at once, with only the pipeline changes that comparison needs. Reader evidence (blind-01 run9): units are distinct inputs, selectable by restricting the prepared input list to original records (the command-line selector has no effect); each unit writes its own result files at the same paths in full and subset runs, with no run-specific content, and its outputs repeat bit for bit; the reproduce logs record every unit's cost; whether a unit reads state left by earlier units of the same invocation is unknown, which the comparison with the frozen baseline tests; units take 1 to 10 min with a cost spread over 50%; the baseline's own threads already use at least half the logical CPUs. Command mode would instead run three whole commands of 1 to 2 h and compare no outputs.

219:- Baseline adapter smoke: after the snapshot and before the test author call, implement runs the baseline adapter evaluate will use (`harness/run_evaluation.sh`, or `harness/run_anchors.sh` when absent) once, as box operation `adapter-smoke` under the method_run budget. Evaluate never passes a subset of the sealed seeds, so the smoke does not either: it is one complete baseline equivalence invocation. The smoke passes when the command exits 0 and `EVAL_OUT/evaluation.json` meets the evaluation record rules: one record per sealed seed and input id, seeds first, then input ids, in sealed order (seed null under a deterministic seal); the sealed `timing_scope`; the sealed `gpu_count`; finite positive `wall_s` for reported timing; and every sealed `equivalence_metrics` name in each record's `metrics` as a finite number.
