221:- wf's optional agent setting `isolation` has `{directory, hidden, box_access}`: an absolute private view directory, an array of absolute paths hidden from that role, and a boolean permitting box credentials. It overrides cwd and add-dirs, disables resume-cache reuse and provider-session export, and is forwarded to every dispatched family, including fallbacks. Real dispatch uses bubblewrap with a read-only host filesystem, private `/tmp`, PID/IPC namespaces, hidden run/workflow paths and provider histories, and a fresh writable HOME containing authentication files only. The view is the only writable host directory. The initial implementer additionally receives read-only access to the existing box wrapper and SSH keys. Test, review and repair roles cannot access them. No sandbox fallback grants broader access: missing bubblewrap or unavailable namespaces fails the call. That outer namespace is the only sandbox: hosts that restrict unprivileged user namespaces (Ubuntu's AppArmor `bwrap-userns-restrict`) deny any namespace nested inside it, so a provider's own sandbox would fail every command. Inside the namespace a Codex agent therefore runs with `danger-full-access`, never `workspace-write` or `read-only`. That mode follows only from the call being dispatched inside the namespace, never from an environment variable: a Codex call outside isolation keeps `workspace-write` or `read-only` even when `CODEX_EPHEMERAL=1` is set. A role whose tools include Write, Edit or Bash keeps the view writable; any other role gets the view mounted read-only, with only its private HOME and temporary directory writable. `WF_STUB` remains an explicit test double, bypassing provider execution. Temporary views/provider state are removed after the stage; raw provider logs remain under the role's workflow transcript directory and are hidden from other roles.
225:- The method author writes three required nonempty files: `method.patch` (git-style paths relative to the published source root), `setup_method.sh`, and `run_method.sh`. An optional fourth file, `run_anchors.sh`, implements the method anchor protocol. No other files are allowed. Shell scripts must pass `bash -n`. The pipeline copies them from the private view into `A/method/`; neither author writes control state.
226:- Each attempt uploads method files to remote `payload/method/` and frozen tests/fixtures to `payload/tests/`. Uploads append independently decodable base64 chunks of at most 24,576 characters, batching commands below 32,768 characters to avoid shell argument limits; each batch has its own receipt. It creates a fresh source copy at `method/` using `cp -a baseline-published method`; patch checking and application use `git apply` with an explicit detached Git context and that copy as work tree, so copied repository/worktree metadata cannot redirect writes into the baseline. A retry always starts from a fresh copy.
227:- The scripts run from the same remote run directory used by reproduce: `bash payload/method/setup_method.sh`, then `bash payload/method/run_method.sh`, then `bash payload/tests/run_tests.sh`. All receive absolute environment paths `BASELINE_DIR` (original published source), `METHOD_DIR` (patched source copy), `BASELINE_OUT` (frozen baseline outputs), and `METHOD_OUT` (remote `out/`). Setup builds the patched copy; run uses the same representative scale, inputs and seeds and writes actual method outputs in exactly the baseline's format and relative output locations. The method author prompt and the method repair prompt list the frozen `method_outputs` paths and state that `run_method.sh` writes each of them under `METHOD_OUT` at that relative path, as the baseline outputs do. After `run_method.sh` exits 0 and its `out/` is fetched, and before any test command, implement checks that every `method_outputs` path exists in that fetched copy as a file or symlink. When any is missing the attempt fails with pipeline failure category `layout` and the tests are not run for that attempt. Fixtures resolve relative to `run_tests.sh`. Remote `out/` is cleared before setup and again before method execution; `out/tests.json` is removed immediately before tests. A previous baseline/method/report cannot satisfy a new attempt.
231:- The test author writes `run_tests.sh`, `outputs.json` and optional fixtures under its private `tests/`. `outputs.json` is exactly `{"method_outputs": [path, ...]}`: a nonempty array of unique relative POSIX paths (no leading `/`, no empty, `.` or `..` segments) naming every file the tests read under `METHOD_OUT`. Each names a regular file under the test view's `baseline-out/`, because the method writes its outputs at the baseline's relative locations. A missing or invalid `outputs.json` fails the test author output like a missing `run_tests.sh`. It is frozen and hashed with the tests. The test author prompt states these rules. Files and nested directories must be regular files/directories, never symlinks or special files; the same restriction applies when copying evidence and method artifacts across views. Scripts must pass `bash -n`. After copying to `A/tests/`, all files become mode 0444 and directories 0555; the pipeline records their tree hash in `C/implement/tests.json` before any method-author call. Remote tests receive the same modes. The pipeline checks the frozen local hash repeatedly and the remote test hash before/after execution, including failed method attempts. Changing tests invalidates blindness and stops the stage without repair.
240:- Each remote integrity command writes `out/implement-state.json`, containing the three baseline/data/output digests above and, once tests are uploaded, `tests_sha256` and `method_payload_sha256` (the uploaded `payload/method/` tree). The latter must remain equal to the pre-execution digest for that attempt, so setup/run/tests cannot replace the uploaded patch or scripts. All are computed from actual remote trees with the committed helper fed to `python3 -I`; method scripts cannot replace a stored helper to forge an integrity check. Control receipts, never model replies, establish these hashes.
283:The harness may additionally provide `A/harness/run_evaluation.sh`, uploaded during reproduce. Otherwise the evaluator uses `harness/run_anchors.sh` for baseline evaluation. The baseline adapter must run the exact published configuration. The method adapter is `payload/method/run_method.sh`. For validity, use optional `payload/method/run_anchors.sh`; absent that file, derive the anchor invocation by running `run_method.sh` with `EVAL_MODE=anchors`. Both routes must rerun the complete published anchor protocol under the method and write `out/anchors_measured.json`; copying baseline or published values is forbidden.
289:- `EVAL_PROTOCOL`: absolute path to the complete immutable sealed predictions JSON, including splits, input pins and seeds. `EVAL_INPUTS` and `EVAL_SEEDS` are JSON encodings of `evaluation_inputs` and `paired_seed_tests`. `EVAL_INPUTS` is an object whose `ids` array lists the sealed input identities in order; each record's `input_id` is one of those strings, and every other key (pins, configuration, generated-input descriptions) describes inputs and is never itself an input. `EVAL_SEEDS` is either `{kind:"paired_median",seeds:[integer,...]}`, whose seeds are the execution seeds in order, or `{kind:"deterministic",...}`, whose single execution seed is null; other keys are descriptive. The harness prompt (which writes `run_evaluation.sh` before the seal exists) and the method author prompt both state these two shapes.
292:Non-anchor adapters write `EVAL_OUT/evaluation.json`:
314:- Before execution all four local verdicts start as `{status:"VOID",reason_code:"not_run"}`. Scorer parse/missing-output failures write `status:"VOID"`, the corresponding `*_pass:null`, and fixed `reason_code:"missing_or_invalid_measurements"`. Invalid manifests use `invalid_manifest`. Earlier raw/phase evidence is retained. Finite measurements are required: zero placeholders never establish PASS.
323:- Both serve and dev `lambda_serve.sh up` write `$HOME/.cache/metis-serve/box.json` atomically alongside `state.json`. Its keys are `{type, region, price_usd_h, started_utc}`: Lambda instance-type and region identifiers, a numeric hourly USD price, and a UTC ISO timestamp. Repeated state saves preserve the allocation's start. Confirmed `down` retains `box.json` and adds `ended_utc` (UTC ISO timestamp) and `hours` (nonnegative elapsed allocation hours, including startup and termination polling). State archival behavior is unchanged. The next `up` replaces this record for the new allocation.
325:- Box receipts add numeric nonnegative `gpu_busy_s` and boolean `gpu_busy_known`. The detached remote script writes `<receipt-id>.gpu` beside its log, sampling `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits` immediately and every 2 seconds until the command exits or times out. Each finite utilization sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100 * 2` seconds; samples from every GPU are summed. Missing/invalid samples contribute nothing. No valid samples means `gpu_busy_s=0`, `gpu_busy_known=false`. Telemetry collection failure does not change command/fetch success. Sampling survives loss of the local polling process; the remote runner stops sampling before publishing its exit marker.
328:- Takeaways facts optionally add `run_box_usd`, a finite nonnegative number or null; old v2 records without this key remain valid. The pipeline writes null for a SKIPPED takeaways stage; otherwise it writes the whole run's box charge here: the intersection of `[run start, takeaways accounting time]` with `[box.started_utc, box.ended_utc]`, multiplied by hourly price. An active box uses accounting time as its end. When timestamps or price are unavailable, it falls back to summed stage USD. This is a run summary, not extra stage spend; takeaways v1 `usd` retains only its own command attribution.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# run_units.sh - the measured baseline restricted to original prepared input records.
     3	#
     4	# Invoked as:  bash harness/run_units.sh <system_id:kind>...   (working directory = the shared run directory, or a sibling
     5	# work directory that links baseline-published/, data/ and harness/). Command paths are relative;
     6	# absolute PATH entries and TMPDIR are inherited from run_command.sh (see REPORT.md).
     7	# PATH entries are resolved from this working directory because the published
     8	# FroDock adapter changes directory into a temporary stage directory.
     9	#
    10	# Representative scale (EXECUTION.json, fixed): the 8 preregistered PINDER-S apo-paired systems in
    11	# data/selection.json; requested holo/apo jobs only, n_solutions=50, mpi_np=8, force=false,
    12	# docked by the published `pinder_methods predict --method frodock` and scored by the published
    13	# `pinder_eval` (50 decoys per selected job). FroDock is CPU + MPI only: no GPU is used (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="",
    14	# GPU count 0). CUDA MPS variables are inherited unchanged.
    15	#
    16	# Output (stdout+stderr of both published commands): out/run_command/run_command.log
    17	#   decoys:  out/results/frodock/<pinder_id>/{holo,apo}_decoys/model_<rank>.pdb
    18	#   scores:  out/results/frodock_metrics.csv, out/results/frodock_leaderboard.csv
    19	# Exit status: nonzero if either published command fails.
    20	set -Eeuo pipefail
    21	[ "$#" -gt 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: at least one system_id:kind is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    22	
    23	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ complete environment
    24	export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""          # CPU/MPI-only baseline
    25	BASELINE_GPU_COUNT=0
    26	N_SOLUTIONS=50
    27	MPI_NP=8
    28	FORCE=false
    29	EVAL_MAX_WORKERS=8
    30	METHOD=frodock
    31	export PINDER_BASE_DIR=data
    32	export PINDER_RELEASE=2024-02
    33	export LOG_LEVEL=INFO
    34	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    35	unset PINDER_DATA_DIR || true
    36	# CUDA toolchain selection (same ls-checked rule as setup.sh; not used by the CPU baseline)
    37	CUDA_SEL=""
    38	for root in /usr/local/cuda /usr/lib/cuda; do
    39	  if ls "$root/bin/nvcc" "$root/include/cuda_runtime.h" "$root/lib64/libcudart.so" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    40	    CUDA_SEL="toolkit_root:$root"; export PATH="$root/bin:$PATH"; export CUDAToolkit_ROOT="$root"; break
    41	  fi
    42	done
    43	if [ -z "$CUDA_SEL" ] && ls /usr/bin/nvcc /usr/include/cuda_runtime.h /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    44	  CUDA_SEL="distro:/usr/bin/nvcc"
    45	fi
    46	[ -n "$CUDA_SEL" ] || { echo "ERROR: no complete CUDA layout found (same rule as setup.sh)" >&2; exit 1; }
    47	VENV=baseline-published/venv
    48	VPY="$VENV/bin/python"
    49	export PATH="$PWD/baseline-published/frodock/bin:$PWD/$VENV/bin:$PATH"
    50	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
    51	
    52	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ output locations (logs preserved)
    53	RUN_DIR="out/run_command"
    54	RESULTS="out/results"
    55	mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history"
    56	TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%NZ)"
    57	if [ -e "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log" ]; then

If the daemon fails to start or any invocation fails under MPS, the probe stops the daemon, records `mps_failed: true`, and repeats the complete probe once without MPS in fresh work directories. Without the binary there is no MPS and `mps_failed` is false.
   104	- MPS use is verified, not assumed. The daemon's `control.log` in its `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` records each client connection as a line containing `NEW CLIENT <pid> from user <uid>`. After each single run and each batch under MPS, the probe counts these lines (case-sensitive substring `NEW CLIENT `, followed by an integer pid and ` from user `). The count must have grown by at least the number of copies just run (1 for a single run, n for a batch of n). A missing or unreadable log, or a smaller increase, means the copies did not run under MPS: the probe treats this like an invocation failure under MPS (stop the daemon, `mps_failed: true`, repeat the complete probe once without MPS). `mps: true` is therefore recorded only when every counted measurement was verified to run under MPS. A single run that exits nonzero stops the probe with a null factor. Before each batch, the batch is skipped when `n * T1` exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. 123: def blob_tree(gs_path: Path, gs: Any = None) -> Generator[str, str, None]:
124:     """Like tree, but for blobs."""
125:     from pinder.core.utils.cloud import Gsutil
126: 
127:     def recurse(obj: dict[str, Any], prefix: str = "") -> Generator[str, str, None]:
128:         contents = dict(sorted(obj.items())).items()
129:         pointers = [_tee] * (len(contents) - 1) + [_last]
130:         for pointer, (name, sub) in zip(pointers, contents):
131:             yield name if not prefix else prefix[4:] + pointer + name
132:             if isinstance(sub, dict):
133:                 extension = _branch if pointer == _tee else _space
134:                 yield from recurse(sub, prefix=prefix + extension)
135: 
136:     if not isinstance(gs, Gsutil):
137:         gs = Gsutil()
138: 
139:     blobs = gs.ls_blobs(gs_path)
140:     root = remote_key(gs_path)
141:     parent = Path(root).parent
142: 
143:     def recursive_defaultdict() -> defaultdict:  # type: ignore
144:         return defaultdict(recursive_defaultdict)
145: 
146:     grouped = recursive_defaultdict()
147: 
148:     for blob in blobs:
149:         path = Path(blob.name)
150:         *nested, name = path.relative_to(parent).parts
151:         sub = grouped
152:         for item in nested:
153:             sub = sub[item]
154:         sub[name] = None
155: 
156:     yield from recurse(grouped)

203:     use_cache: bool = True,
204:     max_workers: int | None = None,
205:     parallel: bool = True,
206: ) -> None:
207:     """Safely copy list of source files to destination filepaths.
208: 
209:     Operates in parallel and assumes that source files all exist. In case any
210:     NFS errors cause stale file stat or any other issues are encountered, the
211:     copy operation is retried up to 10 times before silently exiting.

221:     max_workers : int, optional
222:         Limit number of parallel processes spawned to `max_workers`.
223: 
224:     """

226:         _safe_copy_file,

    48	- Optional `args.harness_from` is a non-empty directory path to a previous run's `A/harness/`, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory. After a successful fresh box probe, the pipeline copies the exact bytes of `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` into the current `A/harness/` and skips the initial harness agent call. If present, `run_evaluation.sh` is copied too. Missing or unreadable required scripts, or an invalid argument, fail reproduce with `error_class: parse`; there is no fallback harness generation. Without this argument, harness generation is unchanged.
    49	- Reuse writes script-owned `C/harness_source.json` as `{source, files}`. `source` is the absolute source harness directory; `files` maps each copied filename to `{sha256, modified}`. `sha256` is the lowercase 64-digit SHA-256 of the exact original copied bytes and remains unchanged after repair. `modified` starts false and becomes true after an accepted repair of that script, before its upload/rerun, even if that rerun fails. Reuse permits the same bounded setup and anchor repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors) as generated harnesses; every repair receives the fresh probe. Reuse adds no stage facts and does not reuse probe results, measurements, or stock verification.
    50	- `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh`, `run_command.sh` are bash scripts. The pipeline invokes them as `bash harness/<name>` from one fresh `/tmp/m5-<uuid>` directory on the already-running operator-managed box. They share that directory across reproduce and profile. No dev lifecycle commands are issued. `BOX` and `FETCH` are inherited unchanged by `boxrun.sh`, including injected executables.
    51	- Harness uploads (the initial upload of every harness script, and the re-upload of rewritten scripts after each accepted repair) use the implement upload encoding, so no process argument or remote command line grows with script size. For each script, the upload truncates `harness/<name>` (`: > harness/<name>`) and then appends its base64 in independently decodable chunks of at most 24,576 characters (`printf %s <chunk> | base64 -d >> harness/<name>`); an empty script is created empty. These lines are batched in order into boxrun commands below 32,768 characters. Every batch begins with `set -e` and `mkdir -p harness out`, runs as operation `upload` under the setup budget, and has its own receipt. A batch that fails (nonzero exit, failed fetch, missing receipt, or a timeout after its identical retry) ends the upload: later batches are not sent and the harness script does not run, and the step fails as a failed upload does today (`infra`, or `timeout` on a timeout). After all batches succeed, the uploaded files are byte-identical to the local harness files. A harness small enough for one batch uploads in exactly one `upload` command, as before. Run evidence (blind-01 run5, 2026-10-31): the single upload command exceeded the operating system's 131,072-byte limit on one argument, spawning boxrun failed with E2BIG before any receipt was written, and reproduce stopped with `infra` before setup ran.
    52	- `setup.sh` installs/builds the exact published baseline in the stock image; sudo is allowed only for apt. Published source/configuration stays under `baseline-published/`; inputs stay under `data/`. Setup builds and checks only the baseline; the fixed pipeline profiler owns profiling tools and installation. Setup must tolerate one retry in the same directory. Tuning is deferred.
    53	- `run_anchors.sh` runs the published protocol at the intake's representative scale and writes `out/anchors_measured.json` as an object mapping each intake item ID (anchors and references) to a finite measured number; with an empty anchors.json it still runs the published command and writes `{}`. Missing or non-numeric measurements fail the corresponding anchor; booleans and nonfinite values count as non-numeric. Additional measurements are ignored for scoring.
    54	- `run_command.sh` contains only the exact measured baseline command and complete environment at the representative scale, including working directory, arguments, CUDA visibility and GPU count. It runs the published binary, saves its output for anchor parsing, and propagates its exit status. `run_anchors.sh` invokes `bash harness/run_command.sh` from the shared working directory without overriding its environment or duplicating the command. Profiling invokes that same file from that same directory. No agent writes profiling scripts or profile outputs.
    55	- `run_command.sh` uses paths relative to its working directory, never absolute paths into the run directory, and writes only under `out/` or temporary files. The concurrency probe and evaluation run it from sibling work directories that link the same trees (see Concurrency probe). Harness and repair prompts state this requirement.
    56	- Optional unit files (U50): `run_units.sh` and `units.json`, used only by the unit equivalence check (U51) and the unit-mode concurrency probe. `units.json` is exactly `{"units": [...]}` with at least four entries, in the order the published full run processes them, each exactly `{id, outputs, cost_s}`: `id` is a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+=-]{0,127}$` that identifies that unit to `run_units.sh`; `outputs` is a non-empty array of unique relative paths naming that unit's result files under `out/`, each one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none of them `.` or `..`; `cost_s` is a finite positive number, the unit's own seconds as recorded in the reproduce run's logs or outputs. `bash harness/run_units.sh <id>...` runs the exact measured command of `run_command.sh` (same binary, configuration, environment and scale) restricted to the listed units (one or more), in the order given, by one of two means: the published program's own subset selection when it takes effect, or otherwise a restricted copy of the prepared input list that the measured command reads, holding only the listed units' original records copied byte for byte in the list's own format, written under `out/` or a temporary directory and passed through an argument, configuration value or environment variable the measured command already accepts. Either way it retains the measured baseline's per-unit code, parameters and inputs exactly as `run_command.sh` runs them, including any documented setup or anchors repairs the measured baseline already carries: the reference is the measured baseline, not the pristine upstream program, and no new code change is allowed. A path-rule conflict that `run_command.sh` already has is inherited and recorded separately; the unit files add none. Reader evidence (run10_diff, 2026-11-01): the entry point's command-line selector exists but has no effect; the measured command reads a prepared input list whose path it already accepts, a restricted list of original records under `out/` adds no write elsewhere, and the per-unit code differences earlier subsetting attempts were flagged for are inherited repairs. Owner decision 2026-11-01: allow selection of original prepared input records while retaining the measured baseline's per-unit code, parameters and inputs. It obeys every `run_command.sh` rule (relative paths, writes only under `out/` or temporary files, no `CUDA_MPS_*` changes), writes each listed unit's `outputs` under `out/` at the same paths as the full run, and propagates the exit status. Under `args.harness_from`, each of the two files present in the source is copied with its exact bytes and recorded in `C/harness_source.json` like the scripts. Files present in `A/harness/` are uploaded with the initial harness upload (same encoding and batching), never later. No repair changes them: after every setup or anchors repair the pipeline restores their bytes (or their absence), as it restores `run_evaluation.sh`. The harness agent is not asked to write them; fresh harness generation is unchanged. The unit equivalence check (U51) and the probe's comparison with the frozen baseline outputs (see Concurrency probe) are their validation.
    57	- The pipeline owns CUDA MPS. No harness script (`setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh`, `run_command.sh`, `run_evaluation.sh`) may set, unset or override any `CUDA_MPS_*` environment variable, or start or stop an MPS daemon; the scripts inherit these variables unchanged. Harness and repair prompts state this rule. (Method code written in implement is not a harness script and may manage MPS itself.)
   122	- Output checks. After `a-1`, every output path of every sample unit under `a-1`'s `out/` must be byte-identical to the same path under the shared run directory's `reproduce-out/` (`baseline_match`); a file missing on either side is a mismatch. When `a-1` exits nonzero or `baseline_match` is false, no later arm runs. After every later invocation, its units' output files must be byte-identical to `a-1`'s (`outputs_match`, true when every later executed invocation matched). An arm counts when all of its invocations exit 0 and all of their compared files match.
   123	- Budget: before each arm, that arm and every later arm are skipped when its estimate exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. The estimate is the sum of the sample's `cost_s` for `a-1`, and `a-1`'s measured wall for every later arm.
   124	- Resource use. For each invocation, from `os.wait4` on its process (which includes its waited-for descendants): `cpu_s` (user plus system seconds), `max_rss_kb`, `nivcsw` (involuntary context switches), `inblock` and `oublock`. 279:     # Close the iterator when returning early so its temporary file is removed.
280:     with closing(iter_manifest(release_url(release))) as records:
281:         for record in records:
282:             if record["key"] == key:
283:                 return record
284:     raise ValueError(f"File absent from release manifest: {uri}")
285: 
286: 
287: def iter_manifest(
288:     root: str, directory: str = ""
289: ) -> Generator[ManifestEntry, None, None]:
290:     """List one flat dataset directory via a release-relative JSONL manifest.
291: 
292:     Manifests live at <release>/manifests/{root,pdbs,mappings,test_set_pdbs}.jsonl.gz
293:     Entries contain a release-relative key, byte size, and base64 MD5. Records
294:     are validated and yielded individually to bound memory use.
295:     """
296:     if directory not in {"", "pdbs", "mappings", "test_set_pdbs"}:
297:         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dataset directory: {directory}")
298:     manifest = f"{root}/manifests/{directory or 'root'}.jsonl.gz"
299:     url = mirror_url(manifest)
300:     with TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
301:         local = Path(temporary) / "manifest.jsonl.gz"
302:         _download(url, local)
303:         with gzip.open(local, "rt") as stream:
304:             for line in stream:
305:                 record = json.loads(line)
306:                 key = record["key"]
307:                 _validate_key(key)
308:                 if str(PurePosixPath(key).parent) != (directory or "."):
309:                     raise ValueError(f"Object outside manifest directory: {key!r}")
310:                 size = record.get("size")
311:                 if type(size) is not int or size < 0:
312:                     raise ValueError("Invalid manifest size")
313:                 try:
314:                     checksum = base64.b64decode(record["md5"], validate=True)
315:                 except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
316:                     raise ValueError("Invalid manifest checksum") from exc
317:                 if len(checksum) != 16:
318:                     raise ValueError("Invalid manifest checksum")
319:                 yield ManifestEntry(key=key, size=size, md5=record["md5"])
320: 
321: 
322: def list_files(root: str, directory: str = "") -> Iterator[str]:
323:     """Yield object URLs from one directory manifest without loading it into memory."""
324:     for record in iter_manifest(root, directory):
325:         yield root + "/" + record["key"]
326: 
327: 
328: def _download_file(source: str, destination: Path) -> None:
329:     url = mirror_url(source)
330:     _, key = _object_key(source).split("/", 1)
331:     if "/" not in key:
332:         record = _root_manifest_entry(source)
333:         _download(url, destination, record["size"], record["md5"])
334:     else:
335:         _download(url, destination)
336: 
337: 
338: def sync_directory(root: str, directory: str, local: Path) -> None:
339:     """Consume a manifest in bounded batches, verifying each missing file."""
340:     records = (
341:         record
342:         for record in iter_manifest(root, directory)
343:         if not (local / PurePosixPath(record["key"]).name).is_file()
344:     )
345: 
346:     def download(record: ManifestEntry) -> None:
347:         _download(
348:             mirror_url(root + "/" + record["key"]),
349:             local / PurePosixPath(record["key"]).name,
350:             record["size"],
351:             record["md5"],
352:         )
353: 
354:     with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=_DOWNLOAD_WORKERS) as pool:
355:         while batch := list(islice(records, _BATCH_SIZE)):
356:             list(pool.map(download, batch))

Sample units have different native basenames, so their native destinations do not automatically collide. Entry-associated shared files could overlap if missing. With all prepared files present and unchanged, shown branches only read and create no such write race. Nothing here establishes another invocation deletes inputs.

No concurrent arm ran in run10, and no concurrency experiment was executed in this audit. Known conditional shared-data writes can be isolated with **per-invocation directory construction**, retaining measured script, configuration and input bytes. This is a prospective orchestration change, not implemented or tested here. A pre-existing private data tree is thus the concrete no-code route for known conditional dataset-write concern. Whether every transitive dependency cache would also need isolation remains unknown; no universal confinement claim follows.

Absolute PATH/TMPDIR spelling conflict remains separate: private directories do not remove absolute spelling, but current-cwd paths and private temp roots do not themselves collide. Prepared shared dataset appears sufficient for known read-only branches, yet declaring whole command harmless would exceed evidence. Status `avoidable_without_code_change=yes`, `avoidance_kind=per_invocation_directory` refers to established conditional shared-data mechanisms; exhaustive runtime-write absence and concurrent success remain unestablished.
